obtained.how: the newspaper's own free web page (Bangor Daily News article page, no paywall met)

bibliography.note: Headline 'The ice is out on Maine's largest lake'; HTML page title 'Moosehead Lake ice-out declared for 2026'; by Susan Bard (BDN outdoors editor); 1 May 2026; section Environment. All as in the reference.

claims.claim: about 61 cm of ice on lower Moosehead Lake in spring 2026 (anglers' reports)
claims.source_value: 24 inches (61 cm) in most areas of the lower lake, one hole close to 28 inches (71 cm), on 8 April 2026
claims.quote: anglers reported 24 inches of ice in most areas on the lower lake
claims.conditions: anglers' reports relayed by MDIFW fisheries resource biologist Jeff Bagley on 8 April 2026; lower Moosehead Lake; not a measured survey
claims.note: 24 in × 2.54 = 60.96 cm ≈ 61 cm. The paper's 'anglers' reports' attribution is right; it could add 'early April' (8 April) and the 71-cm maximum hole.

notes: Other content usable elsewhere: ice-out on Moosehead declared 8:30 a.m., Friday 1 May 2026, by Currier's Flying Service; record earliest 14 April 1945, latest 29 May 1878; recent ice-outs 4 May 2020, 16 Apr 2021, 28 Apr 2022, 25 Apr 2023, 20 Apr 2024, 29 Apr 2025; the call depends on whether the steamship Katahdin can travel Greenville to Northeast Carry (per Maine Public, as quoted). The article says a full list back to 1848 is 'included below', but no list was in the fetched page text.
